Otherwise, whether to roll the transaction back or commit it is yours to decide.

column5: It runs on the connection that its source gives, under the default timeout of the driver, and gives its command no transaction.  It can still run in a transaction of your code's in two cases: On PostgreSQL, on a connection on which your code has begun a transaction, Npgsql runs the command in that transaction.  This holds for a borrowed connection, and for an open connection that a factory returns.  Inside a `TransactionScope`, a connection opened inside the scope takes part in the ambient transaction, whether the method, a factory or your code opened it, unless its connection string turns enlisting off.  A connection opened before the scope does not.  On PostgreSQL, a data source with `Multiplexing=true` cannot take part: Npgsql throws when the connection is opened.
